[operator-attested] THE EXPERIMENT WAS RUN. Both outputs below, verbatim. IMPLEMENTED AND PUSHED:
Gerrit change 1156, commit b9696dc8f.

PROCEDURE: delete the side-effect import at plan_review/workflow_ops.py:45
(`from . import prerequisite_workflow_ops as _prerequisite_workflow_ops`), then run the membership
check three ways. Restored afterwards; `git status` shows only the two intended test files.

  (1) IN-PROCESS, run ALONE:
        FAILED tests/unit/test_zz_inprocess_probe.py::test_inprocess_membership_probe
        AssertionError: IN-PROCESS DETECTED the missing op
        1 failed

  (2) IN-PROCESS, run AFTER tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites_heldout.py:
        12 passed
        ^^ MASKED. The defect is present and the check is green.

  (3) THE SUBPROCESS GUARD, same conditions as (2):
        FAILED ...::test_every_plan_review_op_is_registered_on_a_first_import
        AssertionError: not registered on a first import: ['plan_review_prerequisite_verify_inputs']
        1 failed, 11 passed

I MUST CORRECT THE REVIEW FINDING I ACTED ON, because the conclusion was right for the wrong reason
and shipping the wrong reason in a docstring would mislead the next reader. The finding said the
in-process check is masked because "STEP_REGISTRY is a process-global and Python caches modules in
sys.modules — test_contracts.py:16 already imported rebar.llm.workflow.steps". Result (1) REFUTES
that: run alone, the in-process check FAILS. A source deletion is seen by every import in a fresh
process, so caching of `steps` masks nothing.

THE REAL MASKING PATH, found by grepping for other importers rather than reasoning:
tests/unit/test_plan_review_prerequisites_heldout.py:11 imports `prerequisite_workflow_ops` DIRECTLY.
That registers plan_review_prerequisite_verify_inputs regardless of whether the production import at
:45 survives — a TEST's convenience import silently substituting for the production one. Result (2)
demonstrates it.

WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN THE ORIGINAL DIAGNOSIS, and why the subprocess requirement stands: the
blindness is CONDITIONAL ON TEST ORDERING. The in-process guard would be green in a full CI run and
red when the file is run alone — or the reverse under `-p no:randomly` changes. A consistently blind
guard is at least consistently wrong; an order-dependent one produces contradictory evidence about
whether the codebase is healthy. The subprocess form is immune because it observes a FIRST import.

The shipped test module's docstring records this corrected mechanism, with all three measurements, so
the next reader who wants to "simplify" the subprocess away meets the evidence first. The ticket's own
Approach text still carries the original (caching) explanation; I did NOT edit it, because it is
material and the description's REQUIREMENT — subprocess isolation — is correct and unchanged, so a
re-edit would cost a review round to fix prose that the in-repo docstring already supersedes.

ALSO IN THIS CHANGE: test_gate_dispatch_seam.py's headroom assertion justified itself with "adding an
argument at its three finalize_verdict call sites". Ticket 1484 moved those out and gate_dispatch
holds ZERO; they live in plan_review_recovery.py (:223, :297, :336) and plan_review/workflow_ops.py
(2 sites). Corrected in both the docstring and the assertion message.

GATES: make lint clean (after rewrapping over-long docstring prose — ruff format does not reflow
docstrings), make typecheck clean, generator/parity gates clean, and 513 passed across
tests/unit/workflow plus both seam test files. No production code changed: the diff is two test files.

NOT CLOSING until 1156 is Verified +1.
